elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states: “Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience upon 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires 90 days' written notice, not 30 days' written notice.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires HDI to refund any prepaid fees on a pro-rata basis.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language provides that HDI may terminate for convenience “only effective at the end of the then-current term,” thereby precluding termination during that term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence expressly permits Customer, defined as the Company, to terminate for convenience at any time.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience right requires 60–90 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Customer must provide 90 days' written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: A Termination Payment is imposed when the Company terminates, and the amendment expressly provides that it “shall not exceed 3 months' fees.”

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause states that HDI may terminate for convenience “only effective at the end of the then-current term.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days' written notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: HDI's termination-for-convenience right is expressly conditioned on “90 days' written notice to Customer.”

result.reason: The redline fully implements the fallback position but not the preferred position because Customer receives only a 90-day notice right and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. The changes are substantively limited to clarifying the parties' convenience-termination rights and capping the existing Termination Payment. The specific restriction that HDI may terminate only at term-end limits the broader earlier bilateral termination language, although retaining that earlier language creates some avoidable redundancy. Drafting quality is also slightly reduced because “3 months' fees” is not defined in the clause despite the existing payment formula being based on Net Sales.
